title: Dense integer-lattice restriction for condensed ell-adic derived invariants
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. For $F=E,\Omega$, put $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$, using all continuous maps on profinite sets [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. For a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $V$, put $V_F(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E V)$ with the finite-dimensional product norm topology. For a topological group $J$, write $\mathcal A_F(J)$ for internal $C_F$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] with an action of the condensed group $S\mapsto C(S,J)$; invariants are the equalizer imposing that action to be trivial, and $R\Gamma_J$ is their ordinary total right derived functor in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $r\geq0$, let $L=\mathbf Z_\ell^r$ with its inverse-limit topology, and let $D=\mathbf Z^r$ with the discrete topology. The homomorphism $\iota:D\to L$ sends the $i$th standard integer basis vector to $1$ in the $i$th $\mathbf Z_\ell$ factor. Let $V$ have a continuous $E$-linear $L$-action. Restriction of actions along $\iota$ and the inclusion of invariant objects induce the canonical derived restriction morphism
$$b_F:R\Gamma_L(V_F)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_D(\operatorname{Res}_\iota V_F).$$
This is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$. Its degree-zero map is the identity after identifying $L$-invariants and $D$-invariants. The morphism is natural in continuous equivariant $E$-linear maps of $V$. For $E\to\Omega$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map], the square formed by $b_E$, $\operatorname{Res}b_\Omega$ and the canonical derived coefficient maps induced by $v\mapsto1\otimes v$ commutes. The coefficient maps use the natural equality of invariants with scalar restriction. For $r=0$ the comparison is the identity $V_F[0]$.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] for $R=C_F$, $J=L$, $H=D$ and $u=\iota$. This constructs the specified $b_F$ from the inclusion of invariant objects, as a natural transformation of additive triangulated functors $D(\mathcal A_F(L))\to D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$. In particular it is compatible with the connecting morphism of a short exact sequence of action modules. The map on $H^0$ is the underived invariant inclusion. We will prove that this very transformation is invertible on $V_F[0]$, rather than choose an isomorphism between the two derived objects.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the dense-lattice input: canonical restriction transformation and its exactness

proof.text: The image of $\mathbf Z^r$ is dense in $\mathbf Z_\ell^r$: every nonempty basic open specifies finitely many residues modulo powers of $\ell$, and each coordinate residue has an integer representative. Let a section $m\in C(S,F\otimes_E V)$ be $D$-fixed after every profinite base change, in the sense of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. For every $s\in S$, its value $m(s)$ is fixed by all constant integer elements. The map $x\mapsto x\cdot m(s)-m(s)$ on $L$ is continuous, and its zero set is closed since $F\otimes_E V$ is Hausdorff. Density makes it zero on all of $L$. Thus for every $T\to S$ and continuous $g:T\to L$, one has $g(t)m(t)=m(t)$ at every $t$, so the sections are equal. Hence $m$ is $L$-fixed. The reverse inclusion is immediate by restricting the action. Consequently the inclusion of invariants is literally the identity on their common submodule.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the dense-lattice input: density and degree-zero normalization

proof.text: First consider $V=E$ with trivial action. The two coordinate-cup morphisms of [lem-sfb-trivial-ladic-derived-exterior] and [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-cup-exterior], with $R=C_F$, have exactly the same source $\mathcal E_{C_F,r}$. Each coordinate character restricts by $a_i(\iota(n))=n_i1_F$. Restriction in [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] therefore sends each degree-one connecting class to the corresponding discrete class and preserves ordered cup products and the unit. On every summand $C_F[-|I|]$ this gives $b_F\chi_{F,r}=\chi_{C_F,r}$; the finite biproduct universal property gives the equality on the whole complex. Both $\chi$ maps are isomorphisms, so $b_F$ is one. For a trivial $d$-dimensional $V$, choose an $E$-basis. Its coefficient module is $C_F^d$, since a continuous map into a finite product is exactly a tuple of continuous maps. Additivity and naturality from the calculus identify its comparison with the finite direct sum of the just-proved comparison. This includes $d=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the dense-lattice input: trivial-representation base case, including every rank and coefficient field

proof.text: For either $J=L$ or $J=D$, a central element $z\in J$ acts as an equivariant endomorphism on every action module. On an equivariant injective resolution $N\to I^\bullet$ it acts termwise, giving a lift of $z_N$. On $\Gamma_J(I^q)$ that lift is the identity, by the definition of invariants. The normalized injective-resolution naturality of [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality], applied to this commuting augmentation square, therefore gives $R\Gamma_J(z_N)=\mathrm{id}$. Such resolutions compute these derived functors by [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. If $z_N-1$ is invertible, its derived image is both invertible and zero (additivity). Thus the identity of $R\Gamma_JN$ is zero and the object is zero. In particular, if any $T_i-1$ is invertible on $V$, its inverse is a finite $E$-matrix, hence extends to an invertible endomorphism on $V_F$; the two derived invariant objects are then both zero. Take $z=\iota(e_i)$ for $L$ and $z=e_i$ for $D$. Their centrality follows from commutativity of these groups.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the dense-lattice input: central-action contraction, an elementary resolution calculation

proof.text: If $U\subseteq V$ is $L$-stable, [lem-sfb-continuous-representation-subquotients] gives continuous finite-dimensional representations $U$ and $Q=V/U$ with their usual topologies and continuous equivariant inclusion and quotient. Choose an $E$-linear splitting of the vector-space quotient. Its continuity follows from [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous], since $E$ is complete and nontrivially valued. After extension to either $F$, a matrix and its inverse between finite product spaces are continuous by the topological field operations. Thus $0\to U_F\to V_F\to Q_F\to0$ is split exact on the underlying condensed modules: on every profinite $S$, composition with the continuous splitting lifts every $Q_F(S)$ section. The splitting need not be equivariant; the inclusion and quotient are equivariant, and exactness in the action categories is checked on underlying modules by the calculus. It follows that this sequence gives a distinguished triangle, and step 1 gives a morphism between its two derived-invariant triangles, with components $b_F(U),b_F(V),b_F(Q)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the dense-lattice input: exact finite-dimensional devissage for both coefficient fields

proof.text: Fix $r$ and use strong induction on $d=\dim_E V$, for both $F$ separately. Dimension zero is step 3. Write $A_i=T_i-1$. An invertible $A_i$ is settled by step 4. If every $A_i=0$, each integer generator acts trivially; density, using the same closed-zero-set argument as step 2, shows that the $L$-action is trivial, so step 3 applies. Otherwise, with the invertible case excluded, some $A_i$ is nonzero and singular. Then $U=\ker A_i$ is nonzero and proper. It is $L$-stable since all action operators commute with $T_i$. Thus $0<\dim_E U<d$ and $0<\dim_E(V/U)<d$. Apply step 5 and the induction hypothesis to these two representations. The transformation is compatible with shifts by the calculus, so [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three] applies to the displayed morphism of distinguished triangles and proves that $b_F(V)$ is an isomorphism. This exhausts the alternatives: every nonzero $A_i$ is either invertible or singular. No simultaneous diagonalization, semisimplicity, or completeness of $\Omega$ is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the dense-lattice input: dimension induction; the kernel case carries the nontrivial-representation argument

proof.text: Naturality of $b_F$ for every continuous equivariant $E$-linear map is the naturality of the canonical transformation in step 1; the basis and subspaces used to prove invertibility do not define this transformation. Let $\varphi:C_E\to C_\Omega$ be postcomposition by $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$, and let $f:V_E\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi V_\Omega$ send a section $v$ to $1\otimes v$. This is equivariant and $C_E$-linear, since both actions use the same matrices over $E$. With $J=L,H=D,u=\iota$, the coefficient-pasting equality in [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] reads exactly $c_D\circ b_E=(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi b_\Omega)\circ c_L$, the square requested in the statement. The coefficient transformations there are induced by $f$ and equality of invariants with scalar restriction. Finally, for $r=0$ both groups and the homomorphism are trivial; the normalized transformation is the identity of $V_F[0]$. The identity on $H^0$ for every $r$ was established in step 2.
